Huawei can't get enough memory for its AI chips, pushing customers onto the black market. A sophisticated smuggling network has sprung up to fill the gap, exploiting a loophole in U.S. export rules.

Huawei is telling some customers to source the memory for its AI chips themselves, effectively pushing buyers onto the black market, The Information reports. The company plans to launch the Ascend 960DT early next year, which it says will double the performance of its current chips. But Huawei's Chinese suppliers can't produce enough High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), and U.S. export rules block direct purchases from Samsung and SK Hynix. Together, those two companies control over 80 percent of the global market.

Smugglers have found a workaround. They bundle HBM with cheap server processors whose performance falls below the export threshold, then ship the packages to China through Hong Kong. Once there, workshops separate the memory chips from the processors. The process is fragile and the error rate is high, but the margins make it worth it.

Smuggled memory prices have surged to $4,000 per unit

Prices for smuggled HBM3E memory have jumped from a few hundred dollars to around $4,000 per unit in just one year, according to a broker in Shenzhen. Each AI chip needs six to eight units, meaning the memory alone can cost up to $32,000.

The black market doesn't run on smuggling alone. Older Nvidia GPUs stripped for parts and excess inventory from chip designers who scrapped projects or cut orders also feed the supply. South Korea's customs authority had uncovered trade violations worth $560 million by May, already surpassing the previous full-year record. A third of that total involved strategic goods like chips exported without proper authorization or with false declarations.

translation.html:
华为无法为其 AI 芯片获得足够的内存，正将客户推向黑市。一个组织严密的走私网络已应运而生，利用美国出口规则中的漏洞填补这一缺口。

据 The Information 报道，华为正告知部分客户自行采购其 AI 芯片所需的内存，实际上将买家推向了黑市。该公司计划于明年初推出昇腾 960DT，并称其性能将达到现有芯片的两倍。但华为的中国供应商无法生产足够的高带宽内存（HBM），而美国出口规则又禁止其直接向三星和 SK 海力士采购。这两家公司合计掌控着全球市场超过 80% 的份额。

走私者找到了一种变通办法。他们将 HBM 与性能低于出口管制门槛的廉价服务器处理器封装在一起，再经香港将这些封装件运往中国内地。抵达后，作坊会将内存芯片从处理器上拆离。这一过程容易出问题，出错率也很高，但利润空间使其值得冒险。

走私内存价格已飙升至每个 4,000 美元

据深圳一名经纪商称，短短一年内，走私 HBM3E 内存的价格已从每个几百美元跃升至约 4,000 美元。每颗 AI 芯片需要六到八个这样的内存单元，这意味着仅内存的成本就可能高达 32,000 美元。

黑市的货源并不只靠走私。被拆解以获取零部件的旧款英伟达 GPU，以及芯片设计商因取消项目或削减订单而留下的多余库存，也在为其提供货源。截至 5 月，韩国海关已查获涉案金额达 5.6 亿美元的贸易违规行为，超过了此前的全年纪录。其中三分之一的金额涉及芯片等战略物资在未经适当授权或虚假申报的情况下出口。
